name: ZED X One GS, narrow lens (4.6 mm)

sources.title: ZED X One GS Datasheet, Rev 2.3 (July 2026), Stereolabs
sources.covers: sensor (1/2.6" 2.3MP global shutter, array 1928 x 1208, 3 um pixels), output resolutions and frame rates, output formats, FOV, focal length, aperture and TV distortion per lens, dimensions, weight, power, IMU, synchronisation, interface

sources.title: ZED X One GS store page, Stereolabs
sources.covers: lens options with FOVs (wide 120 x 110 x 80, narrow 91 x 80 x 52 degrees D x H x V), hardware synchronisation and trigger through GMSL2

note: A monocular global-shutter GMSL2 camera with a BMI088 IMU (not modelled), for custom stereo pairs or surround vision. The FOV is the datasheet's "Max." figure; the native resolution is taken as the stated array size 1928 x 1208 (the FOV's image size is not said). Streams: 1920 x 1200 at 60 fps, 1920 x 1080 at 60 fps (cropping mode), 960 x 600 at 120 fps (binning mode), RAW10 over V4L2 (NV21 through Argus). The lens model is pinhole, a labelled ASSUMPTION: the maker states no projection or distortion coefficients; calibrate a unit and store its K and D in the sensor calibration. power_w 0.89 W (12 V, via GMSL2). size_mm read with the long side along the optical axis (the lens), an ASSUMPTION. Narrow lens: 73 (H) x 45 (V) x 87 (D) degrees, focal length 4.6 mm, f/2.0, TV distortion "-6.7% <"; 31 x 31 x 49.3 mm, 50 g. The sources disagree: the store page gives the narrow lens as 91 (D) x 80 (H) x 52 (V) degrees; the datasheet figures are entered. FOV consistency: the maker's angles disagree with the lens geometry by up to 2.25°: on the 1928 × 1208 image a centred lens without pincushion distortion keeps the diagonal angle (87°) at most the vertical angle × diagonal / H (84.8°). That is within the makers' stated FOV tolerance of about ±3° and their rounding (validation check library.fov_shape), so the angles are kept as stated.

sync.what: Datasheet: "Hardware synchronization for multiple connected cameras at frame-level within 15 microseconds"; store page: "Multi-camera hardware synchronization and trigger through GMSL2".
